inhibitors.tip: Tea or coffee right after meals can block iron absorption. Wait 60–90 minutes before having tea.
Dairy calcium can interfere with iron absorption. Try spacing dairy and iron-rich meals by 2 hours.
Calcium supplements reduce iron absorption. Take them at different times of day.

enhancers.tip: Great choice! Vitamin C from citrus helps your body absorb more iron from plant sources.
Tomatoes and peppers are rich in vitamin C, which boosts iron absorption significantly.
Excellent iron-rich choice! Jaggery, dates, and raisins are traditional iron sources.
Green leafy vegetables are iron-rich. Pair with lemon or tomato for better absorption.

defaultTip: Pair iron-rich foods like spinach, jaggery, or dates with vitamin C sources like lemon or amla for better absorption.

iron_deficiency.defaultTip: Likely iron-deficiency pattern: pair dal, palak, or jaggery with lemon/amla, and keep tea 60–90 minutes after meals.

b12_folate.defaultTip: Macrocytic pattern: include B12/folate foods such as eggs, curd (away from iron meals), and dark leafy greens — this does not change the severity badge.

chronic_disease.defaultTip: Normocytic pattern: keep iron-rich meals with vitamin C, and take this sheet to a clinician — type hints never override WHO/ICMR severity.

healthy.defaultTip: CBC pattern looks typical: keep pairing iron-rich foods with vitamin C to maintain levels.

enhancers.tip: For children: a pinch of moringa powder in porridge or daliya is an easy iron boost. Add a squeeze of lemon if the child likes it.

child.defaultTip: For children: stir a pinch of moringa powder into porridge or dal, and offer lemon, amla, or tomato with meals — not tea.

bihar.defaultTip: In this region, sattu, lal saag, and gur with lemon or amla are practical iron-friendly swaps.
